reference.role: 外部舞台空间、材质与正面视角参考；非编辑目标

prompts.title: 错台景深
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a premium wide 16:9 artwork asset for a literary creation studio named Parhelion Theatre. NO text, logos, interface, books or people. This is an extraordinarily beautiful real opera-stage production photographed from the centre of the stalls, exactly FRONT ON, eye-level, full proscenium and apron visible. Input image 1 is a reference ONLY for substantial theatrical architecture, rich tangible curtains, grounded stage floor and frontal viewing angle. Completely redesign its interior: no red moon, no picture-window triptych. Use immaculate crafted scenic design, tactile painted plaster, carved timber, translucent resin, silk scrims, patinated brass; cinematic photographic material realism with subtle painterly colour, absolutely not cheap glossy fantasy CG.
IMPORTANT: Show three DIFFERENT large-scale, freestanding PHYSICAL SCENERY GROUPS on the same deep stage. Each built scenery group is a separate story world. They remain distinct through staggered placement, sculpted riser edges, pockets of unlit stage and narrow angled velvet wing legs, NOT through dividing pillars, three arches, rectangular frames, glass partitions or flat panels. The audience must see three-dimensional scenery: visible side faces and undersides, steps receding into depth, thick ground forms, occlusion, cast shadows and contact shadows, coherent scale and perspective. One continuous outer proscenium only. No tiny toy dioramas, no dollhouse, no model photograph, no isometric view. These are monumental full-size opera sets, filling 70% of the stage opening; reserve only the lower 18% for a beautiful grounded apron with a few footlights.
The SAME three worlds must all read clearly: (1) STAR OBSERVATORY HARBOUR, indigo and muted champagne brass, a tangible curving staircase, elevated stone quay and huge delicate armillary instrument with dark starcloth behind; (2) GLACIAL RIFT, glacier-white and pale violet, bulky translucent sculpted ice cliffs, actual deep chasm with visible rocky ledges and a tall narrow bridge whose supports and underside are visible; (3) MOUNTAIN FOREST, mineral jade and warm coral accents, monumental sculpted tree roots, terraced rock, hanging foliage and layered distant mountain shapes. Do not mix the worlds' objects or continuous landscapes. Every group has its own little ground volume and distinct horizon/depth; no full-width fog uniting the three.
Signature PARHELION: a single elegant engineered solar lighting crown fully visible inside the upper theatre opening, warm opal central sun lens and two smaller companion lenses on a fine aged-brass rail. Recognizable physical stage lighting system, NOT planets, not a moon, not a crystal chandelier. Restrained ivory, cool violet and soft jade shafts visibly pick out the corresponding sets; realistic raking light makes their volumes legible. Sophisticated sumptuousness by measured composition and material quality. Avoid busy filigree, confetti, sparkles, lasers, rainbow haze, portal frames, flat landscape prints, chaotic set clutter, glossy gold everywhere.
COMPOSITION 01 — STAGGERED SCENIC ROSTRA. A broad restrained oxblood velvet proscenium with old champagne-gold details. Central observatory is the main scenic mass, tall and slightly farther back, with broad stairs and a projecting curving quay casting a long shadow onto the apron. Ice landscape sits lower left and slightly forward, its bridge runs diagonally BACK into its own narrow scenic depth. Forest sits right, on a higher irregular terrace that steps down toward the near right edge, very clear root and boulder volumes. The gaps between groups are irregular, 1–2 metres of bare charcoal stage partially hidden by angled silk wings, never rigid vertical boundaries. Shared ground-level raking light anchors every group. Blue-black quiet recesses between worlds make them separate yet theatrically natural. Grand immersive scale, a 12-metre-high set; world scenes are NOT distant views through doorways.

COMPOSITION 02 — THREE SCENIC DECKS ON A REVOLVING STAGE. Dark midnight-blue silk side curtains, refined ivory-stone outer arch and selective antique brass. Seen straight on, three large asymmetric scenic decks sit on a broad shallow circular theatre turntable. Front edges of the decks are tactile curved timber/plaster with visible 40cm thickness and different elevations, separated by slender dark floor channels; no upright walls between them. The central forward deck contains the large forest world, spreading sculpted roots and a multi-level stone stair whose far end disappears into its own green-black wing. Left rear deck is the tall star harbour, a sweeping elevated jetty and brass armillary with physically supported stone piers. Right rear is the glacial canyon, thick crystalline ridges and a constructed bridge facing back-right, deep violet beneath. Space between decks is quiet and stage-like. The solar optical rail hangs just beneath the top curtain and illuminates each scene separately. Elevated scenic elements must be structurally believable and full size, no miniatures. Sensuous curves and solid sculptural weight, three independent episodes in one living theatre.

COMPOSITION 03 — SCENIC WINGS AND RAKED STAGE. A pale warm-stone and dark aubergine silk outer theatre frame, with restrained fine brass moulding. A deep gently raked stage uses staggered slim velvet side-wings turned diagonally rather than upright partitions, THREE large physical sets arranged as an uneven rhythm, without any inner arches. Central forward glacial bridge and massive ice walls dominate, clear hand-worked frosted resin edges, stone foundation, steps descending into a dark rift. Left set is a tall mineral-jade tree with broad mossy stepped roots, deep mountain silhouettes and coral foliage behind its own slanted wing. Right set is the indigo observatory, built stone spiral stairs and a copper-brass orbital instrument on a projecting raised quay, with a midnight star cloth far behind. Enough bare charcoal floor and shadow wedges between the groups to keep their worlds separate, but their boundaries are irregular and scenic. Delicate translucent theatrical silk at upper rear catches the solar lighting without becoming a projection screen. The upper parhelion optical crown is the second visual anchor, fully inside the crop. More quiet and sculptural than baroque; lavish through broad silk folds, solid volumes and considered pools of light. All three sets have near, mid and far spatial planes with truthful cast shadows.
